query: What exact formulas and definitions will we use for string-stability indices, speed-variance reduction, and fuel/emission proxies, and what sample sizes give required statistical power?

response.query: What exact formulas and definitions will we use for string-stability indices, speed-variance reduction, and fuel/emission proxies, and what sample sizes give required statistical power?
response.answer: String-stability indices use the Lyapunov exponent formula; speed-variance reduction employs the standard deviation formula; sample sizes for required statistical power typically use n ≥ 30 for normal distributions.
